nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the complete board is the finite set of edges of the complete graph $K_n$ on the vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$, that is, the set of all unordered pairs $\{i, j\}$ of distinct vertices $i \ne j$.
nodes.title: Edges of the complete graph $K_n$

nodes.summary: For finite sets $X$ (the board), $M$ (the elements claimed by Maker) and $R$ (the elements claimed by Breaker), the free elements are the elements of $X$ claimed by neither player, that is, the set $X \setminus (M \cup R)$.
nodes.title: Free elements of a position

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a set $C$ of unordered pairs of vertices from $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ meets the Hamiltonicity target when the simple graph on these $n$ vertices whose edges are the pairs of distinct vertices in $C$ is Hamiltonian: it has a cycle passing through every vertex exactly once, with the convention that the one-vertex graph is Hamiltonian.
nodes.title: Maker's Hamiltonicity target

nodes.summary: Consider the $(1 : b)$ Maker-Breaker game on the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ in which Breaker moves first: Breaker claims $b$ free edges per turn (all remaining free edges if fewer than $b$ are left), Maker claims one free edge per turn, and Maker wins if, once every edge is claimed, his edges contain a Hamilton cycle. nodes.summary: Fix a finite board $X$, a bias $b \in \mathbb{N}$ and a property of finite sets, Maker's target. At a position $(M, R)$, where $M$ and $R$ are the sets claimed so far by Maker and by Breaker, an element of $X$ is free if it lies in neither $M$ nor $R$. nodes.title: Maker can force a win in the biased Maker-Breaker game

nodes.summary: For a finite board $X$, a bias $b \in \mathbb{N}$ and a target property of Maker's claimed set, Maker wins the $(1 : b)$ Maker-Breaker game on $X$ in which Breaker moves first when, for every set $F \subseteq X$ of exactly $\min(b, |X|)$ elements that Breaker may claim in his first move, Maker can force a win when it is his turn at the position where he has claimed nothing and Breaker has claimed $F$.
nodes.title: Maker wins the biased game with Breaker moving first

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
